## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py` still reads that file, so `load_defaults()` will raise `FileNotFoundError` at runtime. That breakage needs fixing before merge. This review read the full pinned diff, `app/parse.py`, `tests/test_parse.py` and `app/startup.py` at the PR head; the tests were read, not run. It also found that `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535 and that `load_config` silently turns every error into `{}`. One verified strength: the new `ms` branch in `parse_timeout` has a test that checks its result (`parse_timeout("1500ms") == 1.5`).

## Changes
The PR adds a millisecond suffix to `parse_timeout`, plus new `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (with an optional `ujson` accelerator) and `normalize_host` helpers, with tests. It also deletes `app/defaults.json` and adds `docs/reviewer.md` and a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json or update load_defaults — Deleting `app/defaults.json` makes every call to `load_defaults()` in `app/startup.py:6` raise `FileNotFoundError`, because that function still runs `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`. Nothing in the diff updates or removes `load_defaults`, and no test covers it, so the test suite will not catch this. — Any startup path that calls `load_defaults()` crashes instead of getting `{"timeout": 30}`. — Fix: Keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `app/startup.py:6` in this PR to stop reading it.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Accept port 65535 in is_valid_port — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False` because the check is `0 < p < 65535`, but the docstring at `app/parse.py:21` promises "a usable TCP port (1-65535)". The added test `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` only checks 0, 1 and 8080, so the upper bound is never tested. — Configs that use port 65535, a valid TCP port, are rejected. — Fix: Use `0 < p <= 65535` and add assertions for 65535 (valid) and 65536 (invalid).
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — load_config hides read and parse errors as {} — When the file is missing, unreadable or holds malformed JSON (for example `{"timeout": 5`), `load_config` returns `{}`, because `except Exception: return {}` swallows `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError` and the JSON decode error. There is no log and no caller signal, and the docstring ("Load the JSON config at path.") does not say a fallback exists. The PR body calls `{}` a "safe default", but the code does not document that, and no test covers the error path. — A typo in a config path or a broken config file silently runs the app with no configuration, and operators get nothing to diagnose. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` if a missing file should mean an empty config, and let parse and permission errors propagate or log them. Document the fallback in the docstring.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Fix normalize_host docstring for empty input — For `h == ""`, the docstring says `normalize_host` "returns None when h is empty", but the code at `app/parse.py:36-37` does `return ""`. — A caller that follows the docstring and checks `is None` will treat an empty host as a real value. — Fix: Either return `None` or change the docstring to say it returns `""`.
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Test the trailing-dot branch of normalize_host — `test_normalize_host_lowercases` only passes `"Example.COM"`, so no test reaches the trailing-dot removal at `app/parse.py:40-41` (for example `"Example.COM."` → `"example.com"`) or the empty-input branch at `app/parse.py:36`. — If the fully qualified suffix handling regresses, no test will fail.
